key_insight: HVOF-sprayed IN625 and NiCr-10SiC coatings are studied as candidate solar-absorbing surfaces, linking thermal performance with optical response for energy applications.
engineering_relevance: The work is relevant for designing durable, high-temperature solar receiver coatings where absorption, oxidation resistance, and sprayed-layer microstructure must be balanced.
method: Prepared IN625 and NiCr-10SiC coatings using high-velocity oxy-fuel (HVOF) spray.
Compared thermal and optical properties of the deposited coatings.
evidence_signal: The abstract indicates a journal study indexed in OpenAlex/Solar Energy, but provides no numerical results or detailed test data.
watch_item: Performance may depend strongly on spray parameters, substrate compatibility, and long-term thermal stability, which are not specified in the abstract.
paper_title: Thermal and optical properties of HVOF sprayed IN625 and NiCr-10SiC coatings for solar applications
